stories.title: Jio Platforms launches Rs 30,213 crore IPO with >Rs 10 lakh crore valuation
stories.summary: Jio Platforms announced a mega initial public offering with an issue size of Rs 30,213 crore and a valuation exceeding Rs 10 lakh crore, which the source describes as India’s biggest‑ever public issue. The offering is positioned as a historic event for Mukesh Ambani’s telecom and digital services group.
stories.why: It gives investors a chance to participate in India’s leading telecom company and could significantly affect sector market capitalisation.

stories.title: India's unemployment rate stays steady at 5% in September
stories.summary: India's overall unemployment rate held steady at 5.0% in September 2026, compared to the previous month. The rural unemployment rate improved to 4.2%, while urban unemployment increased slightly to 6.9%.
stories.why: This matters because it can affect economic growth, prices, employment, borrowing costs or trade decisions.
stories.previousTitle: India’s unemployment rate steady at 5% in September 2026
stories.previousSummary: The Economic Times reported that India’s overall unemployment rate held at 5.0% in September 2026, unchanged from the previous month. Rural unemployment fell to 4.2%, while urban unemployment rose to 6.9% and urban female unemployment increased to 9.2%. Labour force participation rose to 55.5% year‑on‑year and the worker population ratio climbed to 52.7%.

stories.title: Rupee at 95.05 per dollar as forward premiums hit four-year high
stories.summary: The Indian rupee moved to 95.05 against the U.S. dollar and forward exchange premiums rose to their highest level in four years, occurring amid recent Reserve Bank of India measures. The Economic Times reported the change, noting the currency’s appreciation, the premium surge, and that it may affect market sentiment.
stories.why: RBI action or currency-market developments can affect rupee volatility, hedging costs and foreign-exchange conditions for businesses and investors.

stories.title: Seven crew missing after drone attack leaves tanker ablaze off Romania's coast
stories.summary: A search and rescue operation involving boats and helicopters is now continuing in rough seas, Romania's authorities say Seven of 12 crew members are missing after a drone attack left a chemical tanker ablaze off Romania's coast on Thursday morning, naval authorities say. Romanian President Nicușor Dan confirmed that the Wine Trader and another chemical tanker in the area, the Yara J, had both been struck by drones - the Yara J on Wednesday.
stories.why: This matters because it could affect economic conditions, trade, technology, public systems or international decisions.
stories.previousTitle: Seven missing after drone strike ignites chemical tanker off Romania
stories.previousSummary: A Romanian search and rescue effort using boats and helicopters is ongoing in rough seas after a drone hit the San Marino‑flagged chemical tanker Wine Trader, 13 nautical miles east of the Danube mouth at Sulina. The vessel reported blasts and fire; seven of its 12 crew members are missing. Romanian President Nicușor Dan said another chemical tanker, the Yara J, had been struck by a drone the day before.

stories.title: India’s September trade deficit expands to $30.21 bn as exports rise 23%
stories.summary: In September, India’s trade deficit widened to $30.21 billion, reflecting a larger increase in imports than in exports. Exports grew 23 % year‑on‑year during the same month, while import growth outpaced this rise, leading to the widened deficit. The gap highlights ongoing challenges in balancing trade flows despite the export rebound.
stories.why: Trade developments can affect currencies, business costs, market access and the external balance of the economies involved.
stories.previousTitle: India’s September trade deficit widens to $30.21 billion despite 23% export rise
stories.previousSummary: India’s trade deficit for September stood at $30.21 billion, according to the Economic Times. In the same month, exports increased by about 23 % compared with the previous period. Despite the export gain, the deficit expanded. The widening reflects that import growth outpaced export growth, putting pressure on the balance of payments.
stories.change: No material change since the previous brief.

stories.title: Student protesters attack government buildings in Albania
stories.summary: Thousands of students have taken to the streets in the Albanian capital of Tirana, attacking several government buildings on the second day of violent anti-government protests. Albania's Deputy Prime Minister ​Albana Koçiu has called for "calmness, self-restraint and maturity" and said "Albania does not need to burn to change".
stories.why: This matters because it could affect economic conditions, trade, technology, public systems or international decisions.
stories.previousTitle: Student protests turn violent in Tirana, targeting ministries
stories.previousSummary: Thousands of students took to the streets in Tirana, Albania’s capital, on the second day of anti‑government protests, moving from a rally outside the Ministry of Education to attacks on several government buildings. Part of the education ministry was set on fire and the prime minister’s office, finance ministry, interior ministry and nearby businesses were also attacked. Deputy Prime Minister Albana Koçiu called for calm, saying “Albania does not need to burn to change.”
